title: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (306 GB MoE) TP8+EP8 on two 96 GB PCIe hosts: A leads 7-16%, attribution is bandwidth/small-message/NUMA — not NCCL large-message bandwidth

hardware.gpus: A: 8x RTX 5090 96GB (modded, 575 W); B: 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB (600 W)
hardware.topology_summary: dual-socket servers, 4+4 GPUs across NUMA nodes
hardware.cpu_numa: B: GPU0+GPU4 dual hotspots (~285 W each) matching NUMA groups; A: GPU0 single hotspot (~358 W)

software.nccl: 2.29.7 bundled with torch 2.13.0+cu130 in the vLLM image; SuperBench microbenchmarks used 2.26.5

model.name: GLM-5.3-Flash (official ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3-Flash, FP8 W8A8 e4m3 dynamic, 306 GiB / 62 shards)
model.quantization: FP8 (MoE experts FP8; NVFP4 variant skipped — not runnable in this stack)

workload.server_notes: TP8 + EP8, max-model-len 131072, gpu-mem-util 0.92, max-num-seqs 256, max-num-batched-tokens 8192, port 8200; load ~675 s; B measured after BIOS interconnect fix (2026-10-22)

variance.note: cache-on means of 3 runs per label (A: 2026-10-22 04:29-06:53 UTC, 34 runs total all rc=0; B: 2026-10-22 09:41-12:24 UTC after BIOS fix); A c32 showed +/-14.28 spread, other labels <0.2%

methodology: vllm bench serve, same matrix and seed as the single-card study; cache-on 3x + cache-off 1x per label; an earlier B-machine run before a BIOS interconnect fix was discarded and re-run
transferable: A leads by 7.0-16.2% across the matrix despite B's higher BF16/FP8 compute (~1.85x/1.68x per microbenchmarks) — for streaming FP8 MoE decode, memory bandwidth (~1792 vs ~1597 GB/s) and small-message all-to-all (1MiB: A 16.03 vs B 13.44 GB/s) dominate

After B's BIOS interconnect fix, 1GiB NCCL busbw is ~99% of A on all four ops (allreduce 40.28 vs 40.61) — large-message interconnect is NOT the differentiator; an earlier claim of a 3.4-4x interconnect gap was pre-BIOS data and is retracted
B shows dual NUMA power hotspots (GPU0+GPU4) vs A's single GPU0 hotspot, matching the 4+4 topology
not_transferable: Absolute numbers (power limits, driver, NCCL 2.29.7 path)
B's remaining gap may include NCCL version/kernel differences (2.29.7 all-to-all not separately benchmarked) — needs profiler isolation
NVFP4 variant of GLM-5.3-Flash was skipped and behaves differently
Max-Q (300 W) SKUs will hit the power wall much earlier (see the three-machine single-card study)
